_comment: Resource baseline for the false-PASS guard in audit-bitblt.ps1.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (2026-10-06 audit finding):
The first version of the guard only checked that module NAMES appear in
the netlist. That cannot catch the failure this project has actually hit
twice: the module is still there, but its logic has collapsed. In the
recorded incident u_bitblt appeared 15192 times in the netlist while
holding only 1 FF and 1 LUT.
So compare RESOURCE COUNTS, not names. Values come from
sys\outflow\bitblt_system.res.csv (columns: FFs, SRLs, ADDs, LUTs,
COMB4s, RAMs, DSP/MULTs).
HOW TO READ THE NUMBERS:
They are a snapshot of a design that is believed correct, used as a
LOWER BOUND (with tolerance), never as an exact target. Legitimate edits
move these numbers around by a few percent; a collapse moves them by
orders of magnitude. The tolerance is deliberately loose so ordinary
changes do not trip it.
This cannot detect a design that was already wrong when the baseline was
taken. It detects REGRESSION, which is the failure mode actually seen.
REFRESHING: after an intentional change, re-run the map flow and update
the numbers here -- but only after confirming the new resource counts are
plausible. Refreshing blindly defeats the purpose.

u_bitblt:bitblt_top.note: three DMA engines plus the line scheduler

u_regs:bitblt_axi_slave.note: 16 registers x 32 bits plus the AXI state machine

u_video_out:bitblt_video_out.note: video timing, AXI read FSM, 128-to-24 splitter

pulse_gen_note: bitblt_pulse_gen legitimately synthesises to about 1 FF / 1 LUT -- it is a
single edge detector. That is also the exact signature of collapsed logic,
